html:
SMTO-FIL-0023 — The file is too large to copy, or the storage allowance is full

GUID: a4849f56-b121-49d8-ba35-92e832a5fc18
Slug: file-quota-exceeded
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • Either the file is bigger than SMTO's copy size limit (64 MB unless your administrator changed it), or your storage allowance on that computer is used up. The copy or save didn't complete.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the file's size. If it is over 64 MB (or the limit your administrator set), ask SMTO to copy a smaller file, or split or compress the file first. Files above the copy size limit are refused before they are sent.
  2. If the file was still being written while SMTO copied it, wait until it has finished changing, then ask SMTO to copy it again. A file that grows during the copy sends more data than SMTO expected, so the copy stops.
  3. If the file is small, ask the person who manages the destination computer whether your storage allowance there is full. When the allowance is full, the computer refuses new data no matter the file size.
  4. If SMTO was copying several files, check which ones already arrived before asking it to try again. Some files may have copied before the limit was reached.

What success looks like

  • The copy finishes and the file at the destination is the same size as the original.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; they can raise the copy size limit if you need larger files. Don't delete other people's files or SMTO's saved data to make room.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • File work exceeded a storage quota or transfer bound: the OS returned EDQUOT, the file exceeds the configured maximum transfer size (GATEWAY_TRANSFER_MAX_FILE_BYTES on the Gateway or AOR_ARTIFACT_MAX_FILE_BYTES on the Server, 64 MiB by default), or received bytes would exceed the transfer's declared size.

What this means

  • The OS returned EDQUOT, the requested transfer exceeds its configured maximum file size, or received bytes would exceed the session's declared size. Why this can happen

  • The OS returned EDQUOT, the requested transfer exceeds its configured maximum file size, or received bytes would exceed the session's declared size.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish user/filesystem quota, max_file_bytes and declared session size; free disk space alone may not fix a configured limit.

How to fix it

  • Compare the file size with GATEWAY_TRANSFER_MAX_FILE_BYTES on both Gateways and AOR_ARTIFACT_MAX_FILE_BYTES on the Server, and check the destination account's disk quota. Raise the specific limit deliberately, reduce the transfer, or wait for a growing source to stop changing; do not delete unrelated data (gateway_core/transfer.TransferProvider._open/_execute, agent_runtime/skills/gateway/copy.py).
  • Resolve the specific quota or transfer-size mismatch, or choose a supported smaller scope; do not delete unrelated data.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended transfer fits the applicable quota and configured/declared bounds.

What not to do
